hacker_news.title: Show HN: Counterbranch – See how your PR changes access control
hacker_news.description: Hi, we just released Counterbranch as a GitHub Action (alpha) and are looking for feedback. The action scans your codebase looking for unintended changes to authorization. This can happen in custom code, endpoints, guards, rbac, abac, policy-as-code files, etc. and can lead to broken access control or data exposure. The scanner doesn't use LLMs and is blazing fast. The results show up as a comment on each pull request so you can maintain and improve authz for any volume of human and agentic coders.

hacker_news.title: Ask HN: What do you think about AI generated slides for conferences?
hacker_news.description: As in many other areas (e.g. code, emails, PRs, blog posts), people have started using LLMs to generate slides for their conference talks (e.g., set of HTML pages as a talk). On the one hand, the slides look tidy, neat, and precise, with infographics, plots, dashboards, and so on. Nothing to complain about. On the other hand, they look, hm, like LLM generated web sites, like soulless, if I may say so. I don't know why, but I don't enjoy reading them, even though they probably provide more value than hand crafted. What's your current take?
